  • In 2026, LEAP, Money20/20, and the UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI widened my interests towards technology, finance, and governance. I became more curious about how an idea is put into practice, who can authorise an action, and who takes responsibility. Courses in sales and entrepreneurial resilience added a business perspective to those questions.
  • My next major academic milestone is completing my A-levels in 2028. Beyond that, I want to find the right path into legal study and professional training. 01 / 04

A journey with more than one chapter

My journey begins with school in Riyadh and continues through independent courses, volunteering, and events that have widened my view of different industries.

It has not followed one unchanging career label. Aviation was a significant early interest; corporate and commercial law is the direction I am now working towards.

The connection

The useful connection is the way I approach learning.

Read the deeper context+

I want to understand the systems behind an outcome and the responsibilities that make them work. That interest has travelled from aircraft and airports to businesses, technology, and the commercial questions around them.

2014

School in Riyadh

Al-Rowad International Schools; school completion is expected in 2028.

2024

Structured independent learning

Crew management, aviation management, and business administration.

2025

Beyond the classroom

School volunteering, aviation events, cybersecurity, aircraft design, and finance.

2026

A broader commercial perspective

IAL study, sales and resilience courses, technology, finance, and AI governance.

2028 · expected

The next academic milestone

Expected A-level completion. Higher education and professional training are future steps.

02 / 04

Completed steps

In 2024, I completed courses in crew management, aviation management, and business administration.

Aircraft design followed in May 2025, and business finance in October. That same year, I volunteered at an AIS graduation ceremony, helping with seating, setup, coordination, and backstage support. Each experience gave me a different way to think about working with people.

The connection

In 2025, I visited the Global Airports Forum, Sand & Fun Aviation Show, and Black Hat MEA.

Read the deeper context+

Aviation events brought me closer to a field I had been exploring, while Black Hat introduced a different set of questions about digital trust. I also completed ten hours of CPD activities at Black Hat, which I wrote about afterwards.

03 / 04

The current chapter

In 2026, LEAP, Money20/20, and the UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI widened my interests towards technology, finance, and governance.

I became more curious about how an idea is put into practice, who can authorise an action, and who takes responsibility. Courses in sales and entrepreneurial resilience added a business perspective to those questions.

The connection

I am now studying International A Levels and exploring a future in corporate law, with particular interests in mergers and acquisitions and private equity.

Read the deeper context+

The current chapter is about preparation: doing the academic work, learning what the profession involves, and finding appropriate opportunities to gain experience.

04 / 04

What lies ahead

My next major academic milestone is completing my A-levels in 2028.

Beyond that, I want to find the right path into legal study and professional training. There are still decisions to make, and I would rather understand the options carefully than choose a route simply because its title sounds impressive.

The connection

I expect my interests to keep developing.

Read the deeper context+

Aviation taught me to look at coordination; technology events made me think about responsibility; business learning made me ask about purpose and value. I want to keep those earlier experiences in view as I work towards law, because they help explain how I arrived here.
